t.1.23.1: Then, at the clear break of day, the two subduers of foes placed Viśvāmitra, who had performed his daily rites, before them and came to the bank of the river.
t.1.23.2: Then all those great-souled sages, firm in their vows, brought up a fine boat and spoke to Viśvāmitra.
t.1.23.3: Let your honor board the boat, attended by the princes. Go by a safe path, and let there be no loss of time.
t.1.23.4: Viśvāmitra said, "So be it," and, having honored those sages, he crossed the river that flows to the ocean, accompanied by the two of them.
t.1.23.5: Then, in the middle of the river, Rāma asked the foremost of sages: "What is this tumultuous sound of water being broken apart?"
t.1.23.6: Having heard the words of Rāghava, filled with curiosity, the righteous-souled one told him the certain truth about that sound.
t.1.23.8: From that lake she flowed forth; she embraces Ayodhyā. Issuing from the lake and fallen from Brahmā's lake, the holy Sarayū is she.
t.1.23.7: O Rāma, on Mount Kailāsa a lake was fashioned by Brahmā with his mind, O tiger among men; therefore this lake is called Mānasa.
t.1.23.9: This incomparable sound of it, born of the churning of the waters, rolls toward the Jāhnavī. O Rāma, with a restrained mind, make your obeisance.
t.1.23.10: Those two exceedingly righteous ones, having bowed to the two rivers, reached the southern bank and went on with swift strides.
t.1.23.12: Ah, how impenetrable is this forest, resounding with swarms of crickets, filled with fearsome beasts of prey and with birds of dreadful cries!
t.1.23.11: Seeing that forest, dreadful in appearance and untrodden, the Aikṣvāka, son of the best of kings, questioned the foremost of sages.
t.1.23.13: It was adorned with birds of many kinds screeching with terrifying cries, with lions, tigers and boars, and with elephants as well.
t.1.23.14: Crowded with dhava, aśvakarṇa and kakubha trees, with bilva, tinduka and pāṭala trees, and with badarī bushes, what, pray, is this dreadful forest?
t.1.23.15: To him the great sage Viśvāmitra, of mighty splendour, said: “Hear, dear child Kākutstha, to whom this dreadful forest belongs.”
t.1.23.16: O best of men, these two prosperous lands, the Maladas and the Karūṣas, formerly existed here, fashioned by the handiwork of the gods.
t.1.23.17: Long ago, Rāma, at the slaying of Vṛtra, when the sin of brahmin-slaying entered the thousand-eyed one, he was overwhelmed by filth and by hunger.
t.1.23.18: Bathing that Indra, the gods and the sages rich in austerity bathed him with pitchers, freeing him of his impurity.
t.1.23.20: When Indra had become stainless, free of defilement and pure, the lord, greatly pleased, granted the region an unsurpassed boon.
t.1.23.19: Having cast here upon the earth the filth and also the kāruṣa born of the great Indra's body, they then attained joy.
t.1.23.22: Seeing that honor bestowed upon the land by the wise Śakra, the gods said to Pākaśāsana, "Well done, well done!"
t.1.23.21: These two prosperous lands, the Maladas and the Karūṣas, bearers of the filth of my body, shall attain renown in the world.
t.1.23.23: These two prosperous lands, the Maladas and the Karūṣas, O subduer of foes, rejoiced for a long time because of their wealth and grain.
t.1.23.25: There is one named Tāṭakā, may good fortune be with you, the wife of the wise Sunda, whose son is the rākṣasa Mārīca, mighty as Śakra in valor.
t.1.23.24: Then, after some time, there was a yakṣī who could take any form at will and who possessed the strength of a thousand elephants.
t.1.23.26: O Rāghava, Tāṭakā, whose conduct is wicked, constantly lays waste to these two lands, the Maladas and the Karūṣas.
t.1.23.28: Relying on the strength of your own arms, slay this woman of wicked conduct, and at my command make this land once again free of thorns.
t.1.23.27: She dwells here, blocking the path, at a distance of more than half a yojana. And it is by this very way that we must go, since this is the forest of Tāṭakā.
t.1.23.29: For no one, O Rāma, is able to come to this land, such as it is, laid waste by the terrible and irresistible Yakṣiṇī.
t.1.23.30: All this has been told to you: how this forest became dreadful, and how it was entirely laid waste by the Yakṣī, who even now does not turn away from it.
